ADDITIONAL_STD_DEDUCTION_AGE_65.note: Separate from and stacked with the OBBBA senior bonus deduction below.

SOCIAL_SECURITY_TAXABILITY.indexingNote: UNINDEXED SINCE 1984/1993 BY STATUTE. Never inflate these in projections.
SOCIAL_SECURITY_TAXABILITY.worksheet: Form 1040 instructions, Social Security Benefits Worksheet

SENIOR_BONUS_DEDUCTION.authority: IRC 151(d)(5) as added by P.L. 119-21 (OBBBA); allowed via IRC 63(b)/(d), NOT in the IRC 62 above-the-line list
SENIOR_BONUS_DEDUCTION.criticalNote: Schedule 1-A computes ONE phaseout amount on line 35 and enters it on BOTH line 36a and line 36b. With two qualifying spouses the household therefore loses 12 cents of deduction per dollar of MAGI, not 6 cents. Full phaseout: 175000 single, 250000 MFJ both 65+.
SENIOR_BONUS_DEDUCTION.openDecision: ROUNDING_POLICY - see PHASE-0 spec section 6. Must be resolved with a citation before shipping.

NIIT.criticalNote: A Roth conversion is NOT net investment income, but it DOES raise MAGI and can therefore pull existing investment income into the tax.

CHARITABLE_NONITEMIZER_DEDUCTION.authority: P.L. 119-21 (OBBBA), effective TY2026; above-the-line deduction for cash gifts by non-itemizers, fixed $1,000/$2,000 (not inflation-indexed), permanent. Cross-verified against multiple independent tax-advisory summaries 2026-08-21; primary statutory text not fetched (egress-blocked). Not yet consumed by the engine.
CHARITABLE_NONITEMIZER_DEDUCTION.note: When itemizing is NOT elected, the 0.5% AGI floor (CHARITABLE_AGI_FLOOR) does not apply; DAF and non-cash gifts are excluded.

ITEMIZED_DEDUCTION_BENEFIT_CAP.authority: IRC 68 as amended by P.L. 119-21 (OBBBA) — the '2/37 rule': disallow 2/37 of the lesser of itemized deductions otherwise allowed or the taxable income in the 37% bracket, capping the benefit at 35 cents/dollar. Effective TY2026. Kicks in at the 37% bracket floors ($640,600 single / $768,700 MFJ). Cross-verified 2026-08-21; not yet consumed by the engine.

QCD_LIMIT.authority: IRC 408(d)(8), inflation-indexed under SECURE 2.0 Act. 2026 limit $111,000/individual ($222,000 MFJ), continuing the progression 2023 $100k -> 2024 $105k -> 2025 $108k -> 2026 $111k. Cross-verified 2026-08-21 against multiple independent sources; confirm against IRS Pub 590-B (2026) at advisor review. Consumed by the legacy projector engine only.

RMD_APPLICABLE_AGE.note: Applicable age derived per birth year. The 1959 statutory drafting glitch was resolved to age 73 by Treasury in the July 2024 final regulations (so 1951-1959 -> 73).
RMD_APPLICABLE_AGE.legacyNote: The pre-fix projector applied age 73 to every household regardless of birth year (a fixed input default). Phase 1 replaces this with the birth-year rule above.

RMD_UNIFORM_LIFETIME_TABLE.note: Distribution period by age at year end. Balance is the prior December 31 value. Roth IRAs are excluded from lifetime RMDs.

RMD_ORDERING.note: The RMD is deemed distributed first and is NOT eligible for Roth conversion. An RMD amount contributed to a Roth is a REGULAR contribution and is an excess contribution (6% IRC 4973 excise) to the extent it exceeds the allowable regular Roth contribution. Absent earned income the allowance is 0.
